vignette_preview:
A man in his late 60s presented with a 4-week history of a rapidly growing left caruncular lesion. Medical and ocular histories were unremarkable.

Ocular examination findings were normal except for an amelanotic, pedunculated mass with an ulcerated surface, arising from the caruncle. There was no evidence of PAM (primary acquired melanosis).
